newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks rally will fizzle out - ING Barings.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks rally will fizzle out - ING Barings.

text.p: The rally in Indian stock markets was fuelled by hopes and will be reversed when the expectations fail to materialise, a foreign securities and broking firm said on Tuesday.
"We believe it is a bear market rally built on a lot of hope and anticipation and will fizzle out in the new year when confronted with disappointing news," ING Barings said in a note.
"We continue to recommend restructuring portfolios and exit from auto, cement, steel," the report said.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index was down 17.08 points, or 0.55 percent, at 3,075.96 in afternoon trade.
The benchmark index has been on the rebound after hitting a three-year low of 2,713.12 on December 4.
ING Barings said "hope, rather than belief" of economic and corporate revival sparked the better sentiment.

It cited "modest front running" in anticipation of "robust Indian allocations" in the first quarter of 1997, support from large foreign institutional investors, hedge funds and speculators for the stocks recovery.
"(But) too many hopes (were) pinned on positive developments on the political front," the report said.
